<strong>À une époque où de nombreux cito: At a time when many citizens get their information mainly from social media, these platforms are becoming attractive terrain for fake news manufacturers. Four years later, the country is preparing for another vote in a completely different context.
Il s’agit en effet du premier scrutin de: It is, in fact, the first election since Elon Musk bought Twitter in 2022 – a network he has renamed X – which raises fears about the influence he could have on Canadian politics. But it is also the first election since Mark Zuckerberg, head of Meta, blocked access to Canadian news on Instagram and Facebook in 2023, and then, a few months ago, laid off the fact-checkers who worked for Meta. Fears of a surge in fake news are therefore growing.
En février dernier, le directeur général: Last February, Canada’s Chief Electoral Officer <l1>wrote to digital platforms</l1> to express his concerns about the impact of social media on Canadian democracy.
Le ministre responsable des Institutions: For its part, Quebec’s minister responsible for Democratic Institutions, Jean-François Roberge, tabled a <l1>bill</l1> on April 3 that would make it illegal to deliberately spread fake news in order to influence an election or reduce the public’s confidence in the electoral process. Offenders would face fines of $1,000 to $10,000 for an individual, and $5,000 to $30,000 for a business or organization. These amounts would be increased for repeat offences.
Une <l1>série d’enquêtes</l1> publiées e: A <l1>series of surveys</l1> published in 2023 by Statistics Canada reveals that nearly two-thirds of Canadians (64%) have little trust in information found on social media, and that 43% feel it is increasingly difficult to tell reality from fiction online. Access to reliable information is therefore a significant issue if we want to ensure that the electoral process is fair and transparent.
Les fausses nouvelles peuvent prendre pl: Fake news can take many forms. It may be information that is entirely or partly made up, or images or videos taken out of context, misleadingly edited or generated by artificial intelligence… The goal is often to sow division, manipulate public opinion or favour a particular political direction.
Leurs commanditaires sont des États, des: Those behind it are states, individuals, companies or groups that, driven by an ideology, rely on new technologies and know how to use social media algorithms to interfere in an election campaign. Their goal is to promote the candidate or political party that matches their interests.
Le 7 avril dernier, le gouvernement cana: On April 7, the Canadian government revealed the existence of a <l1>coordinated interference attempt</l1> in the federal campaign, orchestrated by the account Youli-Youmian, considered the most-followed source of information on the Chinese platform WeChat. According to the Security and Intelligence Threats to Elections Task Force, this disinformation operation took place on March 10 and 25, reaching between one and three million views.

Les messages diffusés faisaient l’éloge: The messages that were shared praised Mark Carney, presenting him as the best opponent to Donald Trump and highlighting his professional background in the financial sector. “The information operation aimed to influence Chinese-Canadian communities in Canada and sought to shape their perception of the prime minister, Mark Carney,” Canadian intelligence services say.
Les personnes d’origine chinoise représe: People of Chinese origin make up 4.7% of the Canadian population, according to the 2021 census, a significant electoral weight, particularly in urban centres like Toronto and Vancouver.

Although some past posts have been linked to Chinese state-owned companies, the Chinese embassy in Ottawa has denied any involvement by the Chinese government in the activities of the Youli-Youmian account. Une légende accompagnant l’une de ces im: A caption accompanying one of these images reads: “Why was Canada’s new Liberal prime minister, Mark Carney, on Epstein’s island with Ghislaine Maxwell and Tom Hanks!!!” The aim is clear: to damage the candidate’s reputation by associating him with figures with heavy legal baggage. Yet all of these images were generated by artificial intelligence. They originally carried a Grok AI watermark indicating their artificial nature, but some internet users deliberately removed it.
Certaines figures publiques peuvent égal: Certain public figures can also be used to take part in this influence strategy by spreading biased or manipulated content. A recent example is the case involving Quebec influencer Lauren Chen and her husband Liam Donovan, who were charged by U.S. prosecutors in September 2024 with receiving $10 million from Russian sources. In exchange, they allegedly used their accounts, including a YouTube channel that then had 580,000 subscribers, to spread pro-Russian content during the 2024 U.S. election.
Les conséquences de ces fausses nouvelle: The consequences of this fake news are not limited to influencing the result of an election. It can deeply damage the credibility of democratic institutions and sow confusion among voters. In 2016, false information circulating on social media not only affected the U.S. presidential election but also helped create a climate of widespread mistrust toward the democratic process.
Face à ce défi, la vérification des fait: In the face of this challenge, fact-checking and media literacy are often cited as solutions to combat disinformation. And that starts with helping everyone learn how to tell real news from fake news.
Pour éviter de tomber dans le piège des: To avoid falling into the fake news trap, here are three simple habits to adopt. After that, it takes only a minute to tell reliable information from misleading information.
Les sujets polarisants comme la politiqu: Polarizing topics like politics, the environment, immigration and health are especially prone to fake news during election periods. These stories have one thing in common: they are surprising, even shocking. The goal of those who share them is to provoke an emotion, positive or negative, such as joy, fear or outrage, to get reactions from the audience (likes, shares, comments) and keep people from taking a step back.
Il y a quelques semaines, une rumeur a c: A few weeks ago, a rumour circulated widely online: Pierre Poilievre, leader of the Conservative Party of Canada and a candidate in the federal election, supposedly had a <l1>personal fortune of $25 million.</l1> The claim got a strong reaction from many internet users who, seeing it as proof that the candidate is an oligarch out of touch with the reality of Canadians, used it as an argument to declare they would not vote for the Conservative leader and to try to convince their fellow citizens to do the same.

A few weeks ago, a rumour circulated widely online: Pierre Poilievre, leader of the Conservative Party of Canada and a candidate in the federal election, supposedly had a personal fortune of $25 million. Photo: screenshot
Or, cette affirmation est fausse. Elle t: But this claim is false. It originates from a website called Pierre Poilievre News, a name that should catch your attention… Despite its low traffic, the site managed to contaminate online search results, to the point of being cited as a source by other automated platforms. The article contains precise figures – with no verifiable source – that are then picked up elsewhere, creating an illusion of credibility. Here, the figures are so big and so baseless that this in itself should set off your critical thinking.
N’oubliez pas que n’importe qui peut pub: Remember that anyone can post messages on social media and that the information there isn’t filtered. Use your critical thinking and common sense when faced with a post that plays on prejudice or sensationalism. It’s an essential first step in arming yourself against disinformation.
Les études consacrées aux comportements: Studies on citizens’ behaviour on social media show that, all too often, people simply share links after having read only a headline or seen an image or video. Mistake! Just as you wouldn’t trust just anyone in real life, you should always check the source of information before sharing it.
La première chose à faire est de cliquer: The first thing to do is click on the profile of the account sharing the information. Is it a recognized, reliable media outlet? An anonymous user? A political figure? A company? Be careful: since it became possible to pay for verification – on Instagram as well as on X – the famous blue badge no longer guarantees that an account is truly verified.
Les sites d’informations reconnus et fia: Recognized, reliable news sites, such as La Converse, Radio-Canada, The Rover, Indigenews or Le Devoir, La Presse, APTN News are good indicators. Be wary of suspicious or little-known sites, especially those with a strange URL that doesn’t end in .com, .ca or .org, or that contains numbers in the middle of the letters. Also, a safe URL usually starts with https://. The absence of contact information on the website is another red flag. At the slightest suspicion, it’s best to be cautious and move on to the next step.
<strong>Chercher d’autres sources pour c: Look for other sources to confirm the information
Si une information est vérifiée, elle se: If information has been verified, it will undoubtedly be relayed by other media outlets or credible figures. Fake news often spreads through a single channel, yet it travels six times faster than real news. And it is 70% more likely to be reshared, researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology found as early as 2018. Yet all it takes is a few seconds and an online search engine to avoid the trap.
Tapez les mots clés de l’information que: Type in the keywords of the story you’re looking for and see whether other reliable sources are also reporting it. If not, or if only two dubious sites share the exact same text or video, it is without a doubt fake news. This simple search can also reveal that the information is authentic but was published several years ago, for example.
En suivant ces étapes, chaque citoyen pe: By following these steps, every citizen can considerably reduce the risk of spreading false information and make sure they make an informed decision when it’s time to drop their ballot in the box.
